escalates; it never merges such a change on its own.

## Article XII — The project's scripts are the interface [CRITICAL]

Every task is a script. Run the script, never a command from inside it: each checks its own
prerequisites, and those checks exist because their absence produced failures that took a day to
find. `scripts/check.sh` is the definition of "will CI pass" — a gate added to CI belongs there
too, and a fitness function proves the two lists are equal rather than believing they are.

There are two interfaces, and which directory a script sits in says which one it is.

[`scripts/`](../scripts/) is the **human's** interface to the application — running, testing,
linting, migrating. Run by a person or by CI. Every task exists there as **one** `.sh` script
over the shared `_lib.sh`; task scripts written in Python are libraries that the `.sh` calls,
not a second entry point to the same task.

The scripts are POSIX and that is a decision rather than neglect
([`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Scripts). Windows is supported through WSL
or Git Bash and through nothing else; a named absence of support is more honest than a second
copy of every script that diverges in the week nobody is looking at it.

[the engine](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/) is the **agent's** interface to
the change *process*. Called by the skills that name it, from the repository root, one
implementation per platform. It ships with those skills — in the plugin, not in this
repository — so that a skill and the script it calls change together, and `skill_lint.py`
breaks the build when they do not. The process's own
commands under [the process's own `bin/`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/bin/) are the bridge — its CI runs a shell script, and
the shell script runs Python. `scripts/` is the application's interface and never calls the
process; what the process may call in `scripts/` is the script contract
([`script-contract.md`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/docs/script-contract.md)).

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the process became independent of the
application it works on: a template ships `scripts/` and a stack profile, the process ships
the process's own commands and reads the profile; two trees, two CIs, one contract between them): a script
in `scripts/` as the bridge from the application's CI into the process. It made the application
depend on the process, in the one direction the split forbids, and it put a gate the process
owns into a list the template's CI keeps.

Neither directory is a place to opt out of anything. Both are covered by `ruff` and
`mypy --strict`; choosing a folder has never been a way to lower the standard here.

## Article XIII — Allowed and forbidden [CRITICAL]

**Allowed.** Python ≥ 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 with Alembic, Pydantic 2, PostgreSQL 16 and
only it ([`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § One engine), `uv` in the range
`>=0.12,<0.13`; TypeScript 5.9, React 19, Vite, TanStack Query, react-hook-form with zod,
Tailwind 4 over CSS design tokens; pytest, pytest-bdd, vitest, testcontainers; Playwright
(Chromium alone) only in `e2e/ui/` — [`design/testing.md`](design/testing.md) § The UI smoke in
a browser.

**Forbidden.** Business logic in routers. `fastapi` or `starlette` imported from `services/`,
`models/` or `schemas/`. `create_all()`. A raw hex colour or a magic pixel size in a component.
A file named `utils.py`, `helpers.py`, `common.py`, `format.ts` or `utils.ts`. Star imports,
with one mechanical exception documented in
[`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md). Unpinned tool versions in a gate. Logging
secrets, tokens or personal data.

## Where the process's own files are named

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the change process left this repository
for the plugin `forge@scalo`. Article XII still holds word for word: a tool the stack
profile refuses is not run by hand, and the process's own commands are the bridge from the
process into Python. What changed is only where those commands come from — they arrive on
PATH with the plugin instead of sitting in a directory of this repository's — so the article's links now name
the repository that ships them. No article was reworded; `spec/ADR/` stays empty until the
first change goes through `/forge:sdd`, and framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
`delta.md`): rewording Article XII to describe a plugin. The article is about not assembling
commands by hand, which is true of every layout, and an article edited to track a directory
would need editing again at the next move.

1	# Invariants
2	
3	Things that must always be true. An invariant has no date and no rejected alternative — if it
4	had one it would be a decision and would belong in [`ADR/`](ADR/).
5	
6	**These identifiers are load-bearing.** An identifier from here is never renamed or reused; a
7	superseded invariant keeps its heading and gains a "Superseded by" line. A hole in the
8	numbering is information, not mess.
9	
10	**But a hole is information only when what was in it can still be read, and one of them fails
11	that.** Gate `G9` is cited in this repository solely as a precedent for withdrawal — in
12	[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Scripts, in `stages.py` and in its test —
13	and **what it held is stated by no document, no comment and no commit**. What is left is the
14	information "something was here" without the information "what", which is exactly as much as
15	no entry at all carries. Hence the rule for the next withdrawal: **a withdrawal is recorded
16	together with one sentence about what the gate held.** `G13` has one (the decision about
17	POSIX scripts: the `.sh` and `.ps1` twins must change in one diff) and that is the pattern;
18	`G9` does not, and can no longer be reconstructed.
19	
20	### The rule, amended for gate names
21	
22	**An identifier whose subject is fixed by a document is never renamed. A gate name is renamed
23	only together with a mapping table that keeps every archived citation readable.** The two are
24	not the same kind of identifier, and treating them as one is what this amendment corrects: an
25	invariant's number is a handle on a *decision*, while a gate's identifier is a handle on a
26	*check that still runs* and is read every time it goes red. A handle nobody can decode is a
27	cost paid on every reading.
28	
29	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the gates were renamed from `G1` to `G20`
30	into descriptive names, which is the one thing the rule above forbids, so the rule is amended
31	here rather than quietly broken; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
32	`delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
33	
34	- **Rename without amending this rule.** The rename would then stand as a violation of a
35	  document saying it cannot happen — which teaches that the rules here are advisory, and that
36	  is more expensive than any gate name.
37	- **Rename and drop the old codes from history.** The audits under `spec/rationale/` and the
38	  notes under `retro/` record what was true on a date. Rewriting their nouns makes them agree
39	  with today at the cost of no longer being records.
40	- **Extend "never renamed" to cover gates explicitly, and keep the numbers.** Consistent, and
41	  it settles the cost in exactly the wrong direction: the identifiers a person reads most
42	  often would be the ones guaranteed to stay unreadable.
43	
44	Consequences: gate names are the single renameable identifier space in this repository, and the
45	price of that is the mapping table in
46	[the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py), where every gate declares the code it
47	carried, held to the register by `test_sdd_spec_lint.py`. `D-*`, `R-*`, `CR-*` and the headings in this file are
48	unchanged: never renamed, never reused.
49	
50	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the forge plugin deleted its `docs/` tree
51	on 2026-09-10 and kept only what the process runs on, so `sdd-reference.md` and its table of
52	old numeric codes exist nowhere; the mapping from a retired code to a gate's name lives in the
53	gate register itself, `spec_gates.py`, where every gate declares the code it carried, and the
54	links here name that. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): leaving
55	links that return 404, or copying the mapping into this document — the second home this section
56	argues against.
57	
58	**What this file holds today.** Deliberate non-goals and the rule about the rules themselves —
59	the things that have no version. The data invariants `D-01`…`D-03` moved out to
60	[`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md); the section below
61	says why.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Data invariants
66	
67	**Moved to [`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md),
68	2026-09-02.** The identifiers `D-01`…`D-03` were not renamed or reused and will not be — after
69	this change the `D-*` space has a single owner.
70	
71	What they held, one sentence each, so the hole can be read without opening the other file —
72	the rule at the top of this document demands exactly that:
73	
74	- **`D-01`** — a domain entity has one row from creation to end, not a copy in an "archive
75	  sheet", where history is destroyed by separation rather than by deletion.
76	- **`D-02`** — a fact belonging to another entity is pointed at, not transcribed; the
77	  exception is a deliberate historical snapshot, which has to be named as one.
78	- **`D-03`** — every primary key is a UUID generated on the application side, never a number
79	  from a sequence ([`design/data-model.md`](design/data-model.md) § Identifiers).
80	
81	**Why they left.** A data invariant is a statement about a system boundary — about what may be
82	relied on without looking inside — and a boundary is a versioned contract (constitution,
83	article VI). This file stayed with what has no version: the rule about the rules themselves,
84	and the deliberate non-goals.
85	
86	**The move closed, in passing, a gap this section used to admit outright.** The previous
87	wording said that `D-01`…`D-03` were held by the data model and by the decision about UUIDs,
88	"rather than by a test that names them". The new home does not accept an invariant without a
89	`**Witness:**` and a `**Kind of evidence:**` line, and the witnesses exist: sweepers over
90	`Base.metadata` in `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py` and a property with a generator in
91	`tests/unit/test_data_invariant_properties.py`.
92	
93	**The editing route has not changed, and does not change for either half.** The rule from
94	§ Deliberate non-goals — "every edit to this file within a change cycle belongs to the
95	convergence round" — is inherited by the new home: the write set of `review-converge` covers
96	`contracts/` for the same reason it covers `spec/`.
97	
98	**Which stage's convergence round writes a new data invariant is settled by its witnesses.** The
99	new home accepts no invariant whose `**Witness:**` names a test that does not exist
100	(`tests/fitness/test_invariant_witnesses.py`). So an invariant decided in design whose witnesses
101	the implementation stage writes is written by the first convergence round after they exist —
102	the `spec_sync` stage's — and until then the design document that decided it states the call,
103	and `spec/design/testing.md` names its witnesses and that round. The user decided it so in
104	`CR-2609-823a` (`Q-21`): "stated in the data model now and written into the data-rules folder at
105	the reconciliation stage, once its tests exist."
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Deliberate non-goals
110	
111	Standing product decisions, not oversights: they bind every change exactly as an invariant
112	does, and that is why they live here. Adding any one of them is a change with its own
113	requirements, not a gap somebody spotted.
114	
115	**Lifting a non-goal has one route, and that route is written here, because its absence cost
116	four authors of one stage.** A non-goal is lifted by **a human decision recorded in a change
117	record** (question and answer in `requirements.md`), and an ADR names it only when it is
118	cross-cutting ([`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR).
119	The striking-out is done by the **stage's convergence round**, in this file and in the same PR
120	as the code, because the author of a design document does not have this path in their write
121	set — and does not have it deliberately: a document standing above `spec/design/**` cannot be
122	changed by what stands below it. A lifted item **stays** with its heading and gains a "lifted
123	by `<CR>`" line together with its former wording; it is never renamed or deleted.
124	
125	**This route applies to the whole file, not only to the striking-out.** **Every edit to
126	`spec/invariants.md` within a change cycle** belongs to the convergence round — lifting a
127	non-goal, adding an invariant, fixing a broken cross-reference. No fan-out author gets this
128	path in their write set; an author who sees a divergence here **reports it as a finding and
129	does not try to fix it**. The rule is in this wording because the previous one — written from
130	a single action — did not catch the second case on the same change.
131	
132	- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles; anybody may
133	  add, amend and delete anything the system stores: any guestbook entry and any to-do task. The
134	  signature under an entry is a claim rather than an identity, and no document or screen may assign it a meaning it does not have. A product
135	  built from this template lifts this non-goal with an ADR and hangs the check on **the router
136	  aggregate** — once, never per router: a router added later would be left open until somebody
137	  happened to remember. Which file that is has one home, and it is
138	  [`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
139	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — this file named the router aggregate by

# Invariants

Things that must always be true. An invariant has no date and no rejected alternative — if it
had one it would be a decision and would belong in [`ADR/`](ADR/).

**These identifiers are load-bearing.** An identifier from here is never renamed or reused; a
superseded invariant keeps its heading and gains a "Superseded by" line. A hole in the
numbering is information, not mess.

**But a hole is information only when what was in it can still be read, and one of them fails
that.** Gate `G9` is cited in this repository solely as a precedent for withdrawal — in
[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Scripts, in `stages.py` and in its test —
and **what it held is stated by no document, no comment and no commit**. What is left is the
information "something was here" without the information "what", which is exactly as much as
no entry at all carries. Hence the rule for the next withdrawal: **a withdrawal is recorded
together with one sentence about what the gate held.** `G13` has one (the decision about
POSIX scripts: the `.sh` and `.ps1` twins must change in one diff) and that is the pattern;
`G9` does not, and can no longer be reconstructed.

### The rule, amended for gate names

**An identifier whose subject is fixed by a document is never renamed. A gate name is renamed
only together with a mapping table that keeps every archived citation readable.** The two are
not the same kind of identifier, and treating them as one is what this amendment corrects: an
invariant's number is a handle on a *decision*, while a gate's identifier is a handle on a
*check that still runs* and is read every time it goes red. A handle nobody can decode is a
cost paid on every reading.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the gates were renamed from `G1` to `G20`
into descriptive names, which is the one thing the rule above forbids, so the rule is amended
here rather than quietly broken; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
`delta.md` in which to declare the edit):

- **Rename without amending this rule.** The rename would then stand as a violation of a
  document saying it cannot happen — which teaches that the rules here are advisory, and that
  is more expensive than any gate name.
- **Rename and drop the old codes from history.** The audits under `spec/rationale/` and the
  notes under `retro/` record what was true on a date. Rewriting their nouns makes them agree
  with today at the cost of no longer being records.
- **Extend "never renamed" to cover gates explicitly, and keep the numbers.** Consistent, and
  it settles the cost in exactly the wrong direction: the identifiers a person reads most
  often would be the ones guaranteed to stay unreadable.

Consequences: gate names are the single renameable identifier space in this repository, and the
price of that is the mapping table in
[the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py), where every gate declares the code it
carried, held to the register by `test_sdd_spec_lint.py`. `D-*`, `R-*`, `CR-*` and the headings in this file are
unchanged: never renamed, never reused.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the forge plugin deleted its `docs/` tree
on 2026-09-10 and kept only what the process runs on, so `sdd-reference.md` and its table of
old numeric codes exist nowhere; the mapping from a retired code to a gate's name lives in the
gate register itself, `spec_gates.py`, where every gate declares the code it carried, and the
links here name that. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): leaving
links that return 404, or copying the mapping into this document — the second home this section
argues against.

**What this file holds today.** Deliberate non-goals and the rule about the rules themselves —
the things that have no version. The data invariants `D-01`…`D-03` moved out to
[`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md); the section below
says why.

---

## Data invariants

**Moved to [`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md),
2026-09-02.** The identifiers `D-01`…`D-03` were not renamed or reused and will not be — after
this change the `D-*` space has a single owner.

What they held, one sentence each, so the hole can be read without opening the other file —
the rule at the top of this document demands exactly that:

- **`D-01`** — a domain entity has one row from creation to end, not a copy in an "archive
  sheet", where history is destroyed by separation rather than by deletion.
- **`D-02`** — a fact belonging to another entity is pointed at, not transcribed; the
  exception is a deliberate historical snapshot, which has to be named as one.
- **`D-03`** — every primary key is a UUID generated on the application side, never a number
  from a sequence ([`design/data-model.md`](design/data-model.md) § Identifiers).

**Why they left.** A data invariant is a statement about a system boundary — about what may be
relied on without looking inside — and a boundary is a versioned contract (constitution,
article VI). This file stayed with what has no version: the rule about the rules themselves,
and the deliberate non-goals.

**The move closed, in passing, a gap this section used to admit outright.** The previous
wording said that `D-01`…`D-03` were held by the data model and by the decision about UUIDs,
"rather than by a test that names them". The new home does not accept an invariant without a
`**Witness:**` and a `**Kind of evidence:**` line, and the witnesses exist: sweepers over
`Base.metadata` in `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py` and a property with a generator in
`tests/unit/test_data_invariant_properties.py`.

**The editing route has not changed, and does not change for either half.** The rule from
§ Deliberate non-goals — "every edit to this file within a change cycle belongs to the
convergence round" — is inherited by the new home: the write set of `review-converge` covers
`contracts/` for the same reason it covers `spec/`.

**Which stage's convergence round writes a new data invariant is settled by its witnesses.** The
new home accepts no invariant whose `**Witness:**` names a test that does not exist
(`tests/fitness/test_invariant_witnesses.py`). So an invariant decided in design whose witnesses
the implementation stage writes is written by the first convergence round after they exist —
the `spec_sync` stage's — and until then the design document that decided it states the call,
and `spec/design/testing.md` names its witnesses and that round. The user decided it so in
`CR-2609-823a` (`Q-21`): "stated in the data model now and written into the data-rules folder at
the reconciliation stage, once its tests exist."

---

## Deliberate non-goals

Standing product decisions, not oversights: they bind every change exactly as an invariant
does, and that is why they live here. Adding any one of them is a change with its own
requirements, not a gap somebody spotted.

**Lifting a non-goal has one route, and that route is written here, because its absence cost
four authors of one stage.** A non-goal is lifted by **a human decision recorded in a change
record** (question and answer in `requirements.md`), and an ADR names it only when it is
cross-cutting ([`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR).
The striking-out is done by the **stage's convergence round**, in this file and in the same PR
as the code, because the author of a design document does not have this path in their write
set — and does not have it deliberately: a document standing above `spec/design/**` cannot be
changed by what stands below it. A lifted item **stays** with its heading and gains a "lifted
by `<CR>`" line together with its former wording; it is never renamed or deleted.

**This route applies to the whole file, not only to the striking-out.** **Every edit to
`spec/invariants.md` within a change cycle** belongs to the convergence round — lifting a
non-goal, adding an invariant, fixing a broken cross-reference. No fan-out author gets this
path in their write set; an author who sees a divergence here **reports it as a finding and
does not try to fix it**. The rule is in this wording because the previous one — written from
a single action — did not catch the second case on the same change.

- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles; anybody may
  add, amend and delete anything the system stores: any guestbook entry and any to-do task. The
  signature under an entry is a claim rather than an identity, and no document or screen may assign it a meaning it does not have. A product
  built from this template lifts this non-goal with an ADR and hangs the check on **the router
  aggregate** — once, never per router: a router added later would be left open until somebody
  happened to remember. Which file that is has one home, and it is
  [`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — this file named the router aggregate by
path, and the path changed when the tree was recut by bounded context; the recut is recorded in
[`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § What a new feature adds, and this document
is edited from the trunk, where no `delta.md` exists in which to call the edit editorial):

- **Update the path and keep it here.** It is the smaller edit and it puts this document back
  in the business of tracking where a file lives — which it would then have to do again on
  every later move. A non-goal is a statement about what the system does not do; the file that
  would enforce it if the non-goal were lifted is a placement fact, and placement facts have
  one home.

- **CSRF protection.** There are no sessions, so there is no cookie or header to forge. This
  project once had a layer that echoed an `X-CSRF-Token` header no service set or checked:
  **it protected nothing and looked to an auditor exactly like protection**. A named non-goal
  is more honest than a stub.
- **Content moderation.** There are no reports, no hiding and no word list.
- **Paging and search.** ~~`GET` returns everything. For an example that is right; `BR-04` has
  already prepared the total order that paging will stand on when it is needed.~~ **Lifted
  outside the SDD process, 2026-08-31**, together with replacing the screen with the mock-up:
  `GET` accepts `q`, `sort`, `limit` and `offset`, and the rule is `BR-05` in
  [`contexts/guestbook.md`](contexts/guestbook.md).

  **The lifting was incomplete for one turn, and that is worth recording.** The rule changed in
  the context, in the contract and in the code, and this item stayed — so a document that binds
  every change was saying something untrue, and no gate caught it. `delta-coverage` holds that a changed
  specification file is covered by a delta; it does not hold that a file which **should**
  change did change. Work outside `/sdd` has no convergence round, which is the only place
  this file may be edited — and that is exactly what was missing.
- **A mobile version.** The screen is a single column up to 860 px and narrows with the
  window, but it is **not designed for a phone**: a mobile view is a separate decision with its
  own requirements, not a scaling of what is there. (Wording corrected 2026-08-31: it spoke of
  a 1440×900 frame, which has not existed since the screen was replaced with the mock-up.)
- **A data retention policy.** An entry, like a to-do task, lives until somebody deletes it. A product storing
  personal data needs a policy here before it can be specified in code.
- **A second database engine.** The application runs on PostgreSQL and only on PostgreSQL
  ([`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § One engine). This is not a lack of
  portability but a refusal to maintain a mode in which a green test says nothing about
  production. A machine without Docker points at its own Postgres; a machine with neither gets

## The manual this document cites has moved

The reference tables it points at travel with the process now — the gate register with its retired codes is [the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py) — and not in `docs/`. `docs/` holds
the documentation of the **system** — setting up the AWS account, deploying, configuring,
operating it — and the manual for the **change process** moved beside the framework it
describes.

live in one place, and this is a pointer to it rather than a second copy; framework changes are
made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): recording the argument again here. See
[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Documentation — where a document goes.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a second time
on the same day: out of the process's old home here and out of this repository, into the plugin that now
carries the process. The relative links this document used named a path no clone of this
template has. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): restating the
gate names here so this document could stop citing anything. The whole point of the citation is

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a third time,

1	# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts
2	
3	A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
4	somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
5	a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
6	other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
7	marked `[CRITICAL]`.
8	
9	This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
10	boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.
11	
12	## Why a contract is written rather than generated
13	
14	A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
15	— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
16	repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
17	so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
18	the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
19	had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
20	says how the refusal is declared now).
21	
22	So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
23	output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
24	generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.
25	
26	**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**
27	
28	- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
29	  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
30	  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
31	- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
32	  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
33	  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
34	  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
35	- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
36	  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
37	- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
38	  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
39	  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.
40	
41	The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
42	dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
43	the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
44	would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
45	template that is five paths, ten operations and twelve schemas — and refusals with codes had
46	to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
47	`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.
48	
49	## Compatibility mode
50	
51	A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
52	after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
53	one of three values in its own `README.md`:
54	
55	| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
56	|---|---|
57	| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
58	| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
59	| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |
60	
61	Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
62	code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.
63	
64	## Four boundaries, three directories
65	
66	| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
67	|---|---|
68	| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
69	| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
70	| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
71	| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |
72	
73	**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
74	gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
75	ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
76	the application does not create the schema itself —
77	[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
78	directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
79	first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
80	beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.
81	
82	## What enforces this
83	
84	| Check | What it holds |
85	|---|---|
86	| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
87	| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
88	| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
89	| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |
90	
91	The first three are cheap and textual. The fourth is the one this directory exists for.
92	The full gate table: [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md).

other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
marked `[CRITICAL]`.

This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.

## Why a contract is written rather than generated

A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries

So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.

**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**

- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.

  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.

- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.

## Compatibility mode

A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or

one of three values in its own `README.md`:

| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
|---|---|
| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |

|---|---|
| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |

gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,

  adopting it whole — and the difference is exactly what the next change needs to know. A
  direction is the half of the boundary that was already obvious from the code.
- **Keep the block-sequence front matter.** It was not merely unread: `frontmatter.py` —
  the repository's only front-matter reader — **refuses** it, because block sequences are
  outside the grammar it accepts. So the header was illegal by this repository's own rule and
  nothing said so, which is what a declaration nobody parses always comes to.
- **Add a second, more permissive parser for context documents.** Two readers of one shape is
  the failure `tests/_golden_set.py` already exists to prevent: the hand-copied twin diverged
  in return type and in exception type before anybody noticed. One reader, one grammar.
- **Nest the neighbour rows as a mapping**, which is what YAML would suggest. The grammar
  takes flat scalars and inline lists on purpose — a header of a few keys does not justify a
  third-party parser in the one package that has to keep working when the environment is
  broken. A colon-separated triple is readable, greppable and parses with `str.split`.

## Deliberate non-goals

Named, so that an absence does not read as an oversight:

- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles. Anybody may
  add, amend and delete any entry. The signature is a claim. A product that needs this starts
  with an ADR and hangs the check on the router aggregate — which file that is has one home,
  [`design/conventions.md`](../design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
- **Moderation.** There are no reports, no hiding and no word list.
- **Search relevance.** A phrase is either in the text or it is not. There is no inflection, no
  synonyms, no ranking — `colour` will not find `coloured`, and results come back in the
  guestbook's order rather than by how well they match. A product that needs this starts with a
  full-text index and an ADR.
- **CSRF protection.** There is no cookie or header to forge, because there are no sessions. A
  protective layer that protects nothing while looking like protection is worse than none — this
  project once had exactly that.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-08, `cr: historical` — the router aggregate's path had two homes;
[`../invariants.md`](../invariants.md) § Deliberate non-goals recorded on 2026-09-07 that a
placement fact has one, and this document was the copy that decision missed, corrected here on
the trunk with no `delta.md` to declare the edit in):

- **Keep naming `app/api.py` here.** True today and wrong on the day the aggregate moves. A
  non-goal says what the system does not do; where the check would hang if the non-goal were
  lifted is a placement fact, and placement facts have one home.

## What proves this

`e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` — scenarios in business language, without a single
HTTP code and without a single path, readable by somebody who does not write code. Every rule
above has its scenario there, and two have several: `BR-02` — one for what moves and one for
what must not; `BR-05` — one each for a match in the signature, a match in the message, case,
a search with no matches, the other end of the guestbook, both numbers, and the fact that
successive pieces cover the guestbook exactly once.

87	
88	One flow in five steps, each of which works on its own:
89	
90	1. **Adding.** A person types one line and adds it. The system stores the task, not done, and
91	   records its moment of adding. It appears first in the list without the person reloading.
92	2. **Reading.** Anybody sees every task on one list, newest first, done and not done alike, as
93	   the tasks are stored at the moment the list is read. Other people's changes appear on the
94	   next reading; nothing pushes them to an open screen. A list with no task on it is empty, not
95	   broken, and says what to do.

97	   is.
98	4. **Correcting.** A person changes a task's text. The state and the place stay as they are.
99	5. **Deleting.** A person asks to delete a task and is asked once to confirm. On confirmation the

101	
102	The one state a task has is switched freely in both directions. There is no other state, no
103	order of states to police, and nothing a task has to pass through.
104	
105	## Business rules
106	
107	### `BR-06` — a task needs text, and no more than 200 code points of it
108

110	normalized, trimmed at both ends, and only then measured. A text that is empty once trimmed is
111	refused, nothing is stored, and the person is told that a task needs text. A text longer than
112	200 code points once normalized and trimmed is refused the same way, and the person is told it
113	is too long.

115	The order is what makes the bound honest. Two hundred and five spaces are an empty text, not a
116	text that is too long; two hundred code points with spaces around them are accepted and stored
117	without the spaces. Whitespace inside the text is content and is kept exactly as typed.
118	
119	**The 200 is this context's own number.** It shares its unit with the guestbook's bounds and
120	nothing else. The guestbook's search phrase is also bounded at 200: that is two rules sharing a
121	number, and moving one moves nothing on the other side.
122	
123	**The screen accepts exactly the texts the application accepts.** It never stops taking a text
124	the application would store — two hundred emoji are two hundred code points however the browser
125	counts them — and it never lets through a text the application would refuse.
126	
127	### `BR-07` — a task is one line
128	
129	A text that, once trimmed, still carries a line break (§ Language) is refused, nothing is
130	stored, and the person is told that a task is one line — a reason of its own, never "empty" or
131	"too long", so the person knows what to change.
132	
133	**A text that is also too long is refused as more than one line.** A text over 200 code points
134	with a line break inside it breaks `BR-06` and this rule at once, and the person is told one
135	reason for it — that a task is one line — on the screen and by the application alike. A pasted
136	line break such as U+2028 is often invisible in a one-line field, while a text's length is there
137	to be seen, so the reason the person cannot find for themselves is the one they are given;
138	`BR-06`'s "too long" is the reason for a text of one line.
139	
140	The rule reads the text after the trim. Every one of the seven characters is also in the trim
141	set, so a line break at either end is removed like a space and is not refused; only a line break
142	left inside the text is. A character that shows nothing but is not in the trim set, such as a
143	zero width space, is content — so a line break beside it is inside the text.
144

146	language's own idea of a line break: the two languages this system is built in disagree about
147	some of them, and a pasted text would then be refused on one side and stored on the other.
148

150	
151	Whatever a request to add a task claims, the new task is not done. A list does not start with
152	finished work nobody did. Its moment of adding is recorded when it is stored and never changes
153	afterwards — not by marking, not by correcting. Example tasks in a new environment follow this
154	rule too: one that is to be shown done is added not done and then marked.
155	
156	### `BR-09` — marking records the state the person chose
157	
158	Marking sets a task done or not done; it does not flip whatever is stored. Marking done a task
159	that is already done leaves it done, and marking not done a task that is already not done leaves
160	it not done. That is what keeps two people whose screens are out of date from undoing each
161	other: both chose done, and the task ends done.
162	
163	Marking never changes the text. Every task in the list shows whether it is done, a done task
164	looks different from a not-done one, and a done task's text stays as readable as any other text
165	on the screen — the floor it clears is the screen specification's.
166	
167	### `BR-10` — the text and the state are two things, changed separately
168	
169	Correcting a task changes its text and nothing else: never its state, never its moment of
170	adding. A done task can be corrected exactly as a not-done one can.
171	
172	**A correction is held to `BR-06` and `BR-07` exactly as an addition is.** A corrected text
173	either of them refuses changes nothing — the task keeps the text it had — and the person is told
174	why, with the reason an addition of that text would get.
175	
176	When two changes to one task meet — both sent before either is answered — **the later change to
177	the same thing wins, and a change to one thing never undoes the other**. Two corrections: the
178	text from the one applied later. Two markings: the state chosen in the one applied later. A
179	correction and a marking: both are kept, whichever was applied first. Nobody is told their
180	change was replaced (§ Deliberate non-goals).
181	
182	This has to hold under concurrency and not only in sequence. A correction that writes back the
183	whole task it read would restore the state it read and silently undo a marking made in between —
184	which passes every test that sends one change after another. No check made before the write can
185	hold it; the data model names the mechanism that does
186	([`spec/design/data-model.md`](../design/data-model.md)).
187	
188	### `BR-11` — the list has one order, and a task keeps its place
189	
190	Every task is on one list — done and not done alike, with no pages and no filter — ordered by
191	moment of adding, newest first. Two tasks with the same moment of adding come back in the same
192	relative order every time the list is read, so **the order is total**; without that, two people
193	could read two different lists from the same stored tasks.
194	
195	Marking and correcting never move a task. "Newest" means the moment of adding, never the moment
196	of the last change: a list reordered by its last change makes a task jump every time somebody
197	ticks it. The list is read in this one direction only.
198	
199	### `BR-12` — the same text twice is two tasks
200	
201	Adding a text identical to a task already on the list stores a second, separate task, and each
202	is marked, corrected and deleted on its own. There is deliberately no uniqueness rule here, so
203	nothing is asked of the store to hold one.
204	
205	The consequence is accepted rather than overlooked: an add whose answer was lost on the way back,
206	and which a person then repeats, leaves two tasks, and a person deletes the one they did not
207	mean. Nothing detects it.
208	
209	### `BR-13` — deletion is permanent, and a task that is gone stays gone
210	
211	A deleted task stops existing: no bin, no undo, no recovery. Every other task is left as it was.
212	Deleting somebody else's task is possible, because without accounts there is no such thing as
213	"my task".
214	
215	**A change aimed at a task that no longer exists changes nothing, creates nothing, and tells the
216	person the task no longer exists** — a marking, a correction and a second deletion alike. A write
217	that created the task again on finding it absent would bring back what somebody deleted, and
218	reporting success for a deletion that was not performed is what makes a person believe they
219	deleted twice.
220	
221	## Deliberate non-goals
222	
223	Named, so that an absence does not read as an oversight. The system-wide ones — no accounts, no
224	moderation, no retention policy, no mobile design — are in
225	[`spec/invariants.md`](../invariants.md) § Deliberate non-goals and are not restated here.
226	
227	- **More than one list, and anything on a task but its text and its state.** No due dates,
228	  priorities, assigned people, categories or notes.
229	- **Search, pages, filters and "clear all done".** Everything is on one list.
230	- **Reordering.** Neither by hand nor by state: a done task is not moved to the bottom or into a
231	  section of its own.
232	- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is read again.
233	- **Telling a person that somebody else's change replaced theirs.** The later change wins
234	  (`BR-10`), silently.
235	- **Recording who added, marked or corrected a task.** There is nobody to record.
236	- **Detecting a duplicate.** The same text twice is two tasks (`BR-12`).
237	- **Undo and restore.** A deleted task is gone (`BR-13`).
238	
239	## Open questions
240	
241	- **Is there a largest number of tasks the list holds?** None is set, and with no pages every
242	  task is read at once. A ceiling is a product decision for a person to take, not one a design
243	  document may introduce.

stored, and the person is told that a task is one line — a reason of its own, never "empty" or
"too long", so the person knows what to change.

**A text that is also too long is refused as more than one line.** A text over 200 code points
with a line break inside it breaks `BR-06` and this rule at once, and the person is told one
reason for it — that a task is one line — on the screen and by the application alike. A pasted
line break such as U+2028 is often invisible in a one-line field, while a text's length is there
to be seen, so the reason the person cannot find for themselves is the one they are given;
`BR-06`'s "too long" is the reason for a text of one line.

The rule reads the text after the trim. Every one of the seven characters is also in the trim
set, so a line break at either end is removed like a space and is not refused; only a line break
left inside the text is. A character that shows nothing but is not in the trim set, such as a
zero width space, is content — so a line break beside it is inside the text.

**The seven are one written set that the screen and the application both read**, never each
language's own idea of a line break: the two languages this system is built in disagree about
some of them, and a pasted text would then be refused on one side and stored on the other.

### `BR-08` — a task is born not done, and keeps its moment of adding

Whatever a request to add a task claims, the new task is not done. A list does not start with
finished work nobody did. Its moment of adding is recorded when it is stored and never changes
afterwards — not by marking, not by correcting. Example tasks in a new environment follow this
rule too: one that is to be shown done is added not done and then marked.

### `BR-09` — marking records the state the person chose

Marking sets a task done or not done; it does not flip whatever is stored. Marking done a task
that is already done leaves it done, and marking not done a task that is already not done leaves
it not done. That is what keeps two people whose screens are out of date from undoing each
other: both chose done, and the task ends done.

Marking never changes the text. Every task in the list shows whether it is done, a done task
looks different from a not-done one, and a done task's text stays as readable as any other text
on the screen — the floor it clears is the screen specification's.

### `BR-10` — the text and the state are two things, changed separately

Correcting a task changes its text and nothing else: never its state, never its moment of
adding. A done task can be corrected exactly as a not-done one can.

**A correction is held to `BR-06` and `BR-07` exactly as an addition is.** A corrected text
either of them refuses changes nothing — the task keeps the text it had — and the person is told
why, with the reason an addition of that text would get.

When two changes to one task meet — both sent before either is answered — **the later change to
the same thing wins, and a change to one thing never undoes the other**. Two corrections: the
text from the one applied later. Two markings: the state chosen in the one applied later. A
correction and a marking: both are kept, whichever was applied first. Nobody is told their
change was replaced (§ Deliberate non-goals).

This has to hold under concurrency and not only in sequence. A correction that writes back the
whole task it read would restore the state it read and silently undo a marking made in between —
which passes every test that sends one change after another. No check made before the write can
hold it; the data model names the mechanism that does
([`spec/design/data-model.md`](../design/data-model.md)).

### `BR-11` — the list has one order, and a task keeps its place

Every task is on one list — done and not done alike, with no pages and no filter — ordered by
moment of adding, newest first. Two tasks with the same moment of adding come back in the same
relative order every time the list is read, so **the order is total**; without that, two people
could read two different lists from the same stored tasks.

Marking and correcting never move a task. "Newest" means the moment of adding, never the moment
of the last change: a list reordered by its last change makes a task jump every time somebody
ticks it. The list is read in this one direction only.

### `BR-12` — the same text twice is two tasks

Adding a text identical to a task already on the list stores a second, separate task, and each
is marked, corrected and deleted on its own. There is deliberately no uniqueness rule here, so
nothing is asked of the store to hold one.

The consequence is accepted rather than overlooked: an add whose answer was lost on the way back,
and which a person then repeats, leaves two tasks, and a person deletes the one they did not
mean. Nothing detects it.

### `BR-13` — deletion is permanent, and a task that is gone stays gone

A deleted task stops existing: no bin, no undo, no recovery. Every other task is left as it was.
Deleting somebody else's task is possible, because without accounts there is no such thing as
"my task".

**A change aimed at a task that no longer exists changes nothing, creates nothing, and tells the
person the task no longer exists** — a marking, a correction and a second deletion alike. A write
that created the task again on finding it absent would bring back what somebody deleted, and
reporting success for a deletion that was not performed is what makes a person believe they
deleted twice.

## Deliberate non-goals

Named, so that an absence does not read as an oversight. The system-wide ones — no accounts, no
moderation, no retention policy, no mobile design — are in
[`spec/invariants.md`](../invariants.md) § Deliberate non-goals and are not restated here.

- **More than one list, and anything on a task but its text and its state.** No due dates,
  priorities, assigned people, categories or notes.
- **Search, pages, filters and "clear all done".** Everything is on one list.
- **Reordering.** Neither by hand nor by state: a done task is not moved to the bottom or into a
  section of its own.
- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is read again.
- **Telling a person that somebody else's change replaced theirs.** The later change wins
  (`BR-10`), silently.
- **Recording who added, marked or corrected a task.** There is nobody to record.
- **Detecting a duplicate.** The same text twice is two tasks (`BR-12`).
- **Undo and restore.** A deleted task is gone (`BR-13`).

## Open questions

- **Is there a largest number of tasks the list holds?** None is set, and with no pages every
  task is read at once. A ceiling is a product decision for a person to take, not one a design
  document may introduce.

1	# Requirements — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done
2	
3	**Change:** CR-2609-823a
4	**Source:** request.md, impact.md, brainstorm.md (answers `Q-1`…`Q-9`), and the answers
5	`Q-10`…`Q-12` recorded in the change record on 2026-09-24
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Anybody who opens the application can reach a second screen, a shared to-do list, add a task
10	of one line, tick it done and back, correct it and delete it, while the guestbook stays where
11	it is and keeps working as it does today.
12	
13	Words used below, none of which is in `spec/glossary.md` yet (giving them a home is the design
14	stage's job): a **task** is one line of text somebody put on the list; **the to-do list** is the
15	one list of tasks every visitor shares; **done** and **not done** are the one state a task has,
16	switched both ways; **the moment of adding** is when the system stored a task. It orders the
17	list and never changes.
18	
19	## Success criteria
20	
21	| Id | Criterion | Baseline | How measured after delivery |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **SC-1** | A person who has never seen the to-do list reaches it from the guestbook, adds a task and finds it at the top of the list, with no instruction. | None. Nobody can add a task today: no to-do concept exists in the specification or in the code (`impact.md` § What is missing). | The requester follows the `uat.md` script on the delivered branch before merging and records pass or fail per step. That is the one look after delivery this template schedules. |
24	| **SC-2** | Two people looking at the list after a reload see the same tasks, in the same order, with the same done marks. | None. The guestbook is the only thing people share today, and it has no state anybody marks. | The requester checks it at UAT with two browser windows (`uat.md`). The scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-3` and `CR-2609-823a/R-9` re-check it on every CI run of the branch. |
25	| **SC-3** | A task ticked done by mistake goes back to not done in one action, and neither action moves it in the list. | None. Nothing the application stores has a state that can be switched (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`: "An entry either exists or it does not"). | A `uat.md` step at UAT, plus the scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-4` on every CI run. |
26	| **SC-4** | A reviewer who opens a freshly created environment sees example tasks on the list without typing any. | A freshly created environment opens today with the guestbook's welcome entries (`golden-set/seed/entries-welcome.json`) and nothing else. | The reviewer opens the first preview of this branch (Actions → Preview), or runs `./scripts/start.sh` on a fresh clone, and counts the example tasks. This is manual because the black box starts with `--no-seed` (`R-11`). |
27	| **SC-5** | A guest who knows the guestbook finds it where it was: the main address still opens it and everything it did before still works. | The main address redirects to the guestbook (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Interactions). The 22 scenarios in `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` pass. | The 22 scenarios of `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` run unchanged on every CI run of this branch. The UI smoke's guestbook tests keep asserting what they assert today; a locator that names the lockup or a navigation link may follow the names the user approves in the mock-up (§ Open questions; Self-check 14; assumed: `A-4`, § Named assumptions). The requester checks at UAT. |
28	
29	## Requirements
30	
31	### R-1: Adding a task — **P1**
32	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want to add a task by typing one line, so
33	that it joins the shared list of things to do.
34	**Why this priority:** Without it there is no list. Every other requirement acts on a task this
35	one creates.
36	**Independent test:** Add one task to an empty list and read the list back.
37	
38	1. The system SHALL present one screen holding one field for a new task's text, with the list of
39	   tasks below that field (`request.md`: "a simple view with a field for adding tasks and a list";
40	   `Q-6`: "right under the field").
41	2. The system SHALL let anybody who opens the to-do list add a task, with no account and no
42	   sign-in.
43	3. WHEN a person submits a text for a new task, the system SHALL store one task holding that
44	   text as `R-2` shapes it, record it as not done, and record its moment of adding.
45	4. WHEN a task has been added, the system SHALL show it first in the list without the person
46	   reloading the screen.
47	5. WHEN a person submits a text identical to the text of a task already on the list, the system
48	   SHALL store a second, separate task (`Q-9`).
49	
50	**Acceptance**
51	- **R-1.1** GIVEN an empty to-do list, WHEN a person adds the task "Water the plants", THEN the
52	  list holds exactly one task, its text is "Water the plants", and it is shown as not done.
53	- **R-1.2** GIVEN a list holding the task "Buy bread", WHEN a person adds "Buy bread" again,
54	  THEN the list holds two tasks with that text, and marking one of them done leaves the other
55	  not done.
56	- **R-1.3** GIVEN a list of two tasks, WHEN a person adds a third, THEN the third is shown first
57	  without the page being reloaded.
58	- **R-1.4** GIVEN a request to add a task that arrives already claiming to be done, WHEN it is
59	  stored, THEN the new task is not done.
60	
61	### R-2: What is not a task is refused — **P1**
62	**Objective:** As a reader of the list, I want empty and over-long texts kept out, so that the
63	list never shows a row with nothing in it.
64	**Why this priority:** It is the other half of `R-1`. Shipping `R-1` without it stores empty
65	rows on the first day.
66	**Independent test:** Submit a text of three spaces and confirm the list is unchanged.
67	
68	1. The system SHALL normalize a task's text to Unicode NFC and trim both of its ends of the
69	   written 30-code-point whitespace set, before it measures the text. This is the rule the
70	   system already applies to every text field it accepts (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend,
71	   on `app/platform/schemas/text.py`; the set is defined in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`).
72	2. IF a task's text is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and
73	   tell the person that a task needs text.
74	3. IF a task's text is longer than 200 code points after normalizing and trimming, THEN the
75	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person that the text is too long.
76	4. WHERE a text, once clause 1 has trimmed it, still carries whitespace other than a line break,
77	   the system SHALL keep that whitespace unchanged.
78	5. The system SHALL accept on the screen exactly the texts the service accepts. The field
79	   SHALL NOT block, cut short or silently stop taking a text the service would store, and the
80	   screen SHALL NOT let through a text the service would refuse.
81	6. IF a task's text, once clause 1 has trimmed it, still carries a line break, THEN the
82	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person, with a reason of its own, that a
83	   task is one line (`Q-11`: "Refuse it, with its own message"). A line break is any of U+000A,
84	   U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029: one written set that the screen and the
85	   service both read, never either language's default (assumed: `A-1`, § Named assumptions).
86	   Every one of them is in clause 1's trim set, so a line break at either end is removed by
87	   clause 1 and is not refused. A character that shows nothing but is not in the trim set, such
88	   as U+200B, is content, so a line break beside it is inside the text (assumed: `A-3`, § Named
89	   assumptions).
90	
91	**Acceptance**
92	- **R-2.1** GIVEN the text "   " (three spaces), WHEN it is submitted as a new task, THEN it is
93	  refused, the person is told why, and the list is unchanged. The same holds for the empty text.
94	- **R-2.2** GIVEN a text of exactly 200 code points, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted
95	  and stored whole. GIVEN one of 201 code points, THEN it is refused and the list is unchanged.
96	- **R-2.3** GIVEN a text of 200 × U+1F600 (200 code points, 400 UTF-16 code units), WHEN it is
97	  typed or pasted into the field and submitted, THEN the screen takes every character and the
98	  service stores the task. GIVEN 201 of them, THEN the screen and the service both refuse it,
99	  for the same reason.
100	- **R-2.4** GIVEN a text of 200 letters, each written as U+0065 followed by U+0301 (400 code
101	  points before normalizing, 200 after), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as
102	  200 code points.
103	- **R-2.5** GIVEN a text of 200 code points with two spaces before it and two after (204 as
104	  typed), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as the 200 code points without
105	  the spaces. GIVEN a text of 205 spaces, THEN it is refused as empty, not as too long.
106	- **R-2.6** GIVEN the text "Buy  two   lamps", WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is stored with its
107	  inner spaces exactly as typed.
108	- **R-2.7** GIVEN the text "Buy bread", a line feed, then "and milk", WHEN it is submitted as a
109	  new task, THEN it is refused with the one-line reason, not as empty or too long, and the list
110	  is unchanged. GIVEN "Buy bread" followed by one line feed, THEN it is accepted and stored as
111	  "Buy bread".
112	
113	### R-3: One shared list, in one order — **P1**
114	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want every task on one list in the order
115	the tasks were added, newest first, so that everybody reads the same list the same way.
116	**Why this priority:** The list is what a person looks at. Without a settled order two people
117	see two different lists, and a task just added gets lost among the others.
118	**Independent test:** Add three tasks, then read the list from a second browser.
119	
120	1. WHEN the to-do list is opened, the system SHALL show every stored task, done and not done
121	   alike, on one list, with no division into pages and no filter (`Q-9`).
122	2. The system SHALL order the list by moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`).
123	3. WHERE two tasks share a moment of adding, the system SHALL show them in the same relative
124	   order every time the list is read, so that the order is total.
125	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, or its text is edited, the system SHALL keep it in
126	   the same position in the list (`Q-4`, `Q-6`).
127	5. WHEN the list is opened or reloaded, the system SHALL show the tasks exactly as they are
128	   stored at that moment, including tasks other people have added, marked, edited or deleted.
129	6. WHEN the list holds no task, the system SHALL say that it is empty, with a sentence about what
130	   to do, and SHALL NOT present it as an error (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Components and their states:
131	   "Emptiness always carries a sentence about what to do").
132	
133	**Acceptance**
134	- **R-3.1** GIVEN the tasks "First", "Second" and "Third", added in that order, WHEN the list is
135	  opened, THEN it shows "Third", "Second", "First".
136	- **R-3.2** GIVEN two tasks with the same moment of adding, WHEN the list is read twice, THEN both
137	  reads show them in the same relative order.
138	- **R-3.3** GIVEN 101 stored tasks, WHEN the list is opened, THEN all 101 are shown on one list,
139	  with nothing to press to see more. (101 is one more than the largest piece the guestbook's read
140	  hands out, and more than its default piece of 20.)
141	- **R-3.4** GIVEN the list "Third", "Second", "First" with "Second" not done, WHEN "Second" is
142	  marked done, THEN the list still reads "Third", "Second", "First". The order is also unchanged
143	  after the text of "Second" is edited.
144	- **R-3.5** GIVEN person A has the list open, WHEN person B adds a task and A reloads the list,
145	  THEN A sees B's task first.
146	- **R-3.6** GIVEN no stored task, WHEN the list is opened, THEN the screen says the list is empty,
147	  with a sentence about what to do, and shows no error.
148	
149	### R-4: Marking a task done and not done — **P1**
150	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to tick a task done, and tick it back if I ticked it by
151	mistake, so that the list says what is left to do.
152	**Why this priority:** It is the point of the request: "mark that a task is done" (`request.md`).
153	**Independent test:** Tick one task done, reload, tick it back, reload.
154	
155	1. WHEN a person marks a not-done task as done, the system SHALL record it as done.
156	2. WHEN a person marks a done task as not done, the system SHALL record it as not done (`Q-2`).
157	3. WHEN a person marks a task, the system SHALL record the state the person chose, whatever
158	   state was stored at that moment: marking done a task already done leaves it done, and marking
159	   not done a task already not done leaves it not done.
160	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, the system SHALL leave its text unchanged.
161	5. The system SHALL show, for every task in the list, whether it is done, and SHALL show a done
162	   task differently from a not-done one (`Q-4`).
163	6. WHILE a task is shown as done, the system SHALL keep its text at or above the contrast floor
164	   every text on screen clears, 4.5:1 against the surface it is painted on
165	   (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens).
166	
167	**Acceptance**
168	- **R-4.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN a person marks it done and reloads the
169	  list, THEN "Buy bread" is shown as done, with the same text, in the same position.
170	- **R-4.2** GIVEN the done task "Buy bread", WHEN a person marks it not done and reloads the list,
171	  THEN it is shown as not done.
172	- **R-4.3** GIVEN "Buy bread" is already done, because another person marked it, while this
173	  person's screen still shows it not done, WHEN this person marks it done, THEN it stays done and
174	  is not switched back to not done.
175	- **R-4.4** GIVEN a list holding one done task and one not-done task, WHEN it is shown, THEN the
176	  two are shown differently, and the done task's text measures at least 4.5:1 against the surface
177	  behind it.
178	
179	### R-5: Two screens and the way between them — **P1**
180	**Objective:** As somebody using the application, I want to move between the guestbook and the
181	to-do list, so that I can find the list without knowing its address while the guestbook stays
182	where it was.
183	**Why this priority:** A to-do list at an address nobody is shown is a list nobody uses.
184	`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column says a second screen "must add navigation here".
185	**Independent test:** From the guestbook, reach the to-do list and come back without typing an
186	address.
187	
188	1. The system SHALL give the to-do list an address of its own, and entering that address
189	   directly SHALL open the list (`Q-5`).
190	2. WHILE a person is on the guestbook screen or on the to-do list screen, the system SHALL offer
191	   a way to reach the other screen without typing an address (`Q-1`).
192	3. WHEN a person opens the application's main address, the system SHALL show the guestbook, as it
193	   does today (`Q-5`).
194	4. The system SHALL NOT say anywhere on its screens that the application has one screen (`Q-1`:
195	   that copy "stops being true").
196	
197	**Acceptance**
198	- **R-5.1** GIVEN the to-do list's own address, WHEN a person enters it in the browser, THEN the
199	  to-do list opens.
200	- **R-5.2** GIVEN the guestbook screen, WHEN a person uses the way to the other screen, THEN the
201	  to-do list opens with no address typed. GIVEN the to-do list screen, the same way leads back
202	  to the guestbook.
203	- **R-5.3** GIVEN the application's main address, WHEN it is opened, THEN the guestbook is shown.
204	- **R-5.4** GIVEN an address the application does not know, WHEN it is opened, THEN the page that
205	  says nothing is there does not claim the application has one screen.
206	
207	### R-6: Editing a task's text — **P2**
208	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to correct a task's text, so that a typo or a changed plan does
209	not mean deleting the task and adding it again.
210	**Why this priority:** The list works without it, because delete and re-add is a workaround, but
211	the user put it in scope (`Q-3`).
212	**Independent test:** Edit one task's text and read it back.
213	
214	1. WHEN a person changes a task's text, the system SHALL store the new text and show it in the
215	   task's place.
216	2. WHEN a task's text is edited, the system SHALL leave the task's state as it is stored at that
217	   moment and leave its moment of adding unchanged (`Q-9`: "Editing changes the text only, never
218	   done or not done").
219	3. WHERE a task is done, the system SHALL let a person edit its text exactly as it does for a
220	   not-done task (`Q-9`).
221	4. IF an edited text is empty after trimming, is longer than 200 code points after normalizing
222	   and trimming, or, once trimmed, still carries a line break, THEN the system SHALL refuse the
223	   edit, keep the task's previous text, and tell the person why (`R-2`).
224	
225	**Acceptance**
226	- **R-6.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bred", WHEN it is edited to "Buy bread", THEN the list
227	  shows "Buy bread", not done, in the same position.
228	- **R-6.2** GIVEN the done task "Call the plumber", WHEN it is edited to "Call the plumber again",
229	  THEN it is still done and in the same position.
230	- **R-6.3** GIVEN the task "Buy bread", WHEN it is edited to "   ", THEN the edit is refused and the
231	  task still reads "Buy bread". An edit to a text of 201 code points is refused the same way. An
232	  edit to a text with a line break between two words is refused the same way.
233	
234	### R-7: Deleting a task — **P2**
235	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to remove a task, with one question before it goes, so that a
236	list does not fill with things nobody will do and a slip of the mouse deletes nothing.
237	**Why this priority:** Useful and independent of every other operation, and in scope (`Q-3`).
238	**Independent test:** Delete one task out of three and confirm the other two remain.
239	
240	1. WHEN a person asks to delete a task, the system SHALL ask them to confirm before it deletes
241	   anything (`Q-9`).
242	2. WHEN the person confirms, the system SHALL delete the task permanently, with no bin, no undo
243	   and no recovery (`Q-9`).
244	3. IF the person does not confirm, THEN the system SHALL leave the task as it was.
245	4. WHEN a task is deleted, the system SHALL leave every other task unchanged.
246	
247	**Acceptance**
248	- **R-7.1** GIVEN the tasks "Alpha", "Beta" and "Gamma", WHEN a person deletes "Beta" and
249	  confirms, THEN the list holds "Alpha" and "Gamma", and "Beta" does not come back after a reload.
250	- **R-7.2** GIVEN the task "Beta", WHEN a person asks to delete it and then cancels, THEN "Beta"
251	  is still on the list, unchanged.
252	
253	### R-8: A task that no longer exists — **P2**
254	**Objective:** As somebody whose screen is out of date, I want to be told clearly when the task I
255	am acting on has been deleted, so that I never believe I changed something that is gone.
256	**Why this priority:** Without identity anybody can delete any task, so this happens as soon as
257	two people use the list. The user asked for "a clear message" (`Q-9`).
258	**Independent test:** Delete a task through one browser, then try to mark it done through
259	another.
260	
261	1. IF a person edits, marks or deletes a task that has already been deleted, THEN the system
262	   SHALL change nothing, create no task, and tell the person the task no longer exists.
263	2. IF the same task is deleted a second time, THEN the system SHALL refuse and tell the person it
264	   no longer exists, rather than report a deletion it did not perform.

266	**Acceptance**
267	- **R-8.1** GIVEN person A's screen shows "Buy bread" and person B has deleted it, WHEN A marks it
268	  done, THEN A is told the task no longer exists, and after a reload no "Buy bread" is on the list.
269	- **R-8.2** GIVEN the same situation, WHEN A saves an edit of "Buy bread" to "Buy rye bread", THEN
270	  A is told the task no longer exists, and no task "Buy rye bread" appears.
271	- **R-8.3** GIVEN a task already deleted, WHEN it is deleted again, THEN the person is told it no
272	  longer exists.

274	### R-9: Two people changing one task at once — **P2**
275	**Objective:** As one of several people sharing the list, I want changes made at the same moment
276	to settle predictably, so that my tick is never silently undone by somebody else's edit.
277	**Why this priority:** It applies only when two people act on one task at once, but when that
278	happens and this requirement is missing, a change is lost with nothing on screen to show it.
279	**Independent test:** Send an edit and a mark for one task before either one is answered.
280	
281	1. WHEN two people change the text of the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL keep
282	   the text from the change applied later (`Q-9`: "the later change wins").
283	2. WHEN one person edits a task's text while another marks the same task at the same moment, the
284	   system SHALL keep both changes, the edited text and the chosen state, in whichever order they
285	   are applied.
286	3. WHEN two people mark the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL end with the state
287	   chosen in the change applied later.
288	
289	"At the same moment" means that both changes are sent before either one is answered.
290	
291	**Acceptance**
292	- **R-9.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B marks it
293	  done, both before either is answered, THEN the task reads "Buy rye bread" and is done, whichever
294	  change was applied first.
295	- **R-9.2** GIVEN the task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B edits it to "Buy
296	  white bread", and B's change is applied later, THEN the task reads "Buy white bread".
297	- **R-9.3** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A and B both mark it done, both before either
298	  is answered, THEN it is done.
299	
300	### R-10: A change that did not go through is not shown as made — **P2**
301	**Objective:** As somebody on a poor connection, I want to know when my change did not go
302	through, so that I never believe a task was added, ticked, edited or deleted when it was not.
303	**Why this priority:** The list belongs to the application, not to the browser (`brainstorm.md`
304	§ What was settled). A screen showing a change the application never stored lies about the one
305	thing the list is for.
306	**Independent test:** Cut the service off, tick a task, and read the screen.
307	
308	1. IF adding, marking, editing or deleting a task is not stored, because the service cannot be
309	   reached or refuses the change, THEN the system SHALL tell the person the change was not made.
310	2. IF a change was not stored, THEN the system SHALL NOT show it in the list as made.
311	3. IF the list cannot be read, THEN the system SHALL say that the list failed to load and SHALL NOT
312	   say that the list is empty.
313	
314	**Acceptance**
315	- **R-10.1** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person marks "Buy bread" done, THEN the
316	  screen says the change was not made and "Buy bread" is shown as not done.
317	- **R-10.2** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person adds a task, THEN the screen says
318	  the task was not added and no new task appears in the list.
319	- **R-10.3** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN the to-do list is opened, THEN the screen
320	  says the list failed to load, and does not show the empty-list sentence of `R-3.6`.
